narrative: OMX30 faces a Friday morning headwind despite remaining +7.1% above its 200-day moving average. Global correlation has turned sharply negative (-0.489%) driven by a US equity rout (S&P -0.87%, Dow -1.32%) and a VIX surge (+7.52% to 16.01), signaling genuine risk-off reorientation. Technical structure remains constructive—bull market regime, positive ROC-90 (+5.0%), price in lower-half Bollinger band with room to mean-revert—but ADX weakness at 6.5 severely undermines conviction. The +0.92% spike in US 10Y yields offers bank NIM support, yet the concurrent Treasury volatility and Bessent headlines create macro uncertainty. With MACD below signal and no clear directional momentum, expect a subdued, choppy session biased toward modest underperformance.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens under pressure from the US selloff and VIX surge; expect range-bound trading around 3120–3145. Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A, Swedbank A) should outperform on the 92bp yield bump and NIM tailwind, partially offsetting equity weakness. Industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo B) face headwinds from risk-off sentiment despite a positive USD/SEK (+0.20%)—exporter support is marginal. Mining (Boliden) is a bright spot with copper +1.29% and gold +1.96%, though oil's -0.55% slide dampens heavy machinery demand. Tech/Telecom (Ericsson B, Hexagon B) pressured by NASDAQ selloff (-1.00%) and weak ADX. Watch US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET—a surprise miss could deepen the selloff. Key support at 3085 (lower Bollinger), resistance at 3180 (50-MA); yesterday's close (3123) is the pivot. Reduce position sizes and avoid aggressive longs until ADX recovers above 18.
